key_insight: MRI radiomic features from pre-operative brain scans added prognostic value beyond clinical variables for lung cancer brain metastases, and the imaging risk groups appeared to reflect underlying immune-tumor biology.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this approach could help identify patients at higher risk of death or leptomeningeal progression and support more personalized follow-up and treatment planning.
method: Retrospective cohort of 103 lung cancer patients with brain metastases and matched MRI/histopathology.
Extracted radiomic features from contrast-enhanced T1 and FLAIR MRI sequences.
Compared Cox models, random survival forests, and DeepSurv using clinical, imaging, and combined inputs for OS, CNS progression, and LM progression.
evidence_signal: The combined clinical-imaging DeepSurv model achieved the best overall survival concordance index (0.728), and imaging-only risk groups showed differences in tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and PD-L1 expression.
watch_item: Single-center retrospective data with a modest sample size means the findings need external validation before routine clinical use.
paper_title: MRI Biomarkers for Brain Metastases in Lung Cancer Using Machine Learning
